input.strategy_title: Bring-your-own vector database for RAG workloads
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

RAG applications built on Llama Stack need a vector store, and today the
platform neither ships one nor documents how to attach an external one.
Customers are split into two camps with incompatible expectations: regulated
customers want a platform-managed vector database with supported images and
lifecycle, while cloud-native customers already run managed services (e.g.
a cloud vector DB) and only want a sanctioned way to connect them. We have not
decided which posture to productize first, and the answer changes most of the
downstream work.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A decision is reached, with a documented evaluation, on the first supported vector store posture: platform-managed (operator-deployed Milvus) versus external-connection-only. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Depending on that decision: either administrators can deploy the managed vector store through the Platform Operator with productized images, or data scientists can register an external vector store connection per project with validated connectivity. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Llama Stack distributions can consume the chosen vector store as a RAG provider without hand-editing distribution configs. |
| HLR-4 | P1 | The Dashboard exposes the chosen integration (deploy-and-manage UI for the managed path, or connection management UI for the external path). |
| HLR-5 | P2 | Product documentation covers setup and limits for whichever posture ships. |

## Affected Components

- Llama Stack
- Dashboard
- Platform Operator

## Out of Scope

- Shipping both postures in the same release
- Embedding model selection and lifecycle (separate strategy)

## Open Questions

1. Managed Milvus versus external-connection-only is genuinely undecided — the
   evaluation in HLR-1 must weigh supportability cost, disconnected-environment
   viability, and time-to-market, and the outcome forks the implementation
   structure for HLR-2 through HLR-5.

# Midstream repo onboarding for the Milvus vector database

## Description

Create the midstream repository for the Milvus vector database under
opendatahub-io, as the foundation for productized, supported Milvus images
used by the platform-managed vector store posture. This epic exists only if
the posture investigation selects the platform-managed path.

## Scope

- Fork/mirror the upstream Milvus repository into a new midstream repo under
  the opendatahub-io organization.
- Establish the midstream conventions: branch strategy relative to upstream,
  import/rebase process, and ownership documentation.
- Provide whatever minimal build scaffolding is needed for the repository to
  produce a buildable container image target for later pipeline onboarding.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A midstream Milvus repository exists under opendatahub-io with documented
  ownership.
- The upstream sync/rebase process is documented and executable.
- The repository contains a buildable image target suitable for the build
  pipeline onboarding that follows.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)** (platform-managed branch): "administrators can deploy the
  managed vector store through the Platform Operator with productized
  images" — this epic provides the repo foundation for those productized
  images.

# License validation for Milvus and transitive dependencies

## Description

Run license scanning and validation for Milvus and its transitive
dependencies so the platform-managed posture can ship productized, supported
images without license exposure. This epic exists only if the posture
investigation selects the platform-managed path.

## Scope

- License scan of the Milvus source and its transitive dependency tree as
  pulled into the productized image.
- Identify any copyleft or otherwise incompatible licenses in the dependency
  set.
- Produce a go/no-go assessment with a remediation plan for any flagged
  dependencies (removal, replacement, or documented acceptance).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A complete license scan report exists for Milvus and its transitive
  dependencies.
- Every flagged license has a documented remediation path or an explicit,
  approved acceptance.
- A go/no-go decision is recorded; if dependencies must change, the finding
  is fed back to the managed-deployment implementation before release.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)** (platform-managed branch): productized images for the
  managed vector store require clean or remediated licensing.

# Konflux build pipeline onboarding for the Milvus midstream image

## Description

Onboard the Milvus midstream repository to Konflux so the platform-managed
posture has a productized, pipeline-built container image. This epic exists
only if the posture investigation selects the platform-managed path, and it
starts once the midstream repository exists.

## Scope

- Create the Konflux application and build pipeline configuration for the
  Milvus midstream repo.
- Wire the image build through the standard onboarding recipe so images are
  produced and published to the product registry.
- Verify the pipeline produces a signed/publishable image artifact.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Konflux application exists for the Milvus midstream repository.
- The build pipeline completes green on the default branch.
- A publishable Milvus container image is produced and available to be
  referenced (by digest) by the managed vector store deployment.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)** (platform-managed branch): "productized images" for the
  managed vector store.

# Platform Operator deployment and lifecycle for the managed vector store

## Description

Extend the Platform Operator so administrators can deploy the managed
Milvus vector store with productized images and platform-managed lifecycle.
This is the core deliverable of the platform-managed posture and exists only
if the posture investigation selects that path.

## Scope

- Add the managed vector store as a deployable capability of the Platform
  Operator: administrator-initiated deployment of Milvus using the
  productized image.
- Cover basic lifecycle concerns within the operator's existing patterns:
  deployment, status reporting, and upgrade handling for the managed
  instance, including its persistent storage needs.
- Reference the productized Milvus image by pinned digest.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An administrator can deploy the managed vector store through the Platform
  Operator without manual manifest editing.
- The deployment uses the productized Milvus image, pinned by digest, with
  the digest available from the image build pipeline (availability of the
  pinned digest is an acceptance gate, not a scheduling dependency — the
  operator implementation proceeds in parallel with image pipeline
  onboarding).
- The operator reports deployment status and handles upgrade of the managed
  instance.
- Persistent storage for the managed vector store works within the
  platform's storage conventions.
- The Platform Operator build pipeline is green for the changes.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)** (platform-managed branch): "administrators can deploy the
  managed vector store through the Platform Operator with productized
  images" — primary coverage.

# Consume the managed vector store as a RAG provider in Llama Stack distributions

## Description

Wire Llama Stack distributions so they consume the platform-managed vector
store as a RAG provider without hand-editing distribution configs. This epic
exists only if the posture investigation selects the platform-managed path,
and it builds on the managed vector store deployment capability being
available.

## Scope

- Automatic discovery/wiring of the managed vector store connection into
  Llama Stack distribution configuration (consistent with the Llama Stack
  provider-plugin model documented in its architecture context), so no
  hand-edited distribution configs are needed.
- Ensure vector RAG workflows (insertion and retrieval) function against the
  managed store through the standard provider interface.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Llama Stack distribution picks up the managed vector store as its RAG
  vector provider with no hand-edited distribution configuration.
- Vector insertion and retrieval workflows function end-to-end against the
  managed store via the distribution.
- The wiring follows the existing provider-plugin configuration model rather
  than introducing a parallel configuration mechanism.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P1)**: "Llama Stack distributions can consume the chosen vector
  store as a RAG provider without hand-editing distribution configs" —
  platform-managed branch coverage.

deploy-and-manage UI, following the Dashboard's existing component
integration patterns. This epic exists only if the posture investigation
selects the platform-managed path.

## Scope

- Dashboard surface for administrators to deploy and manage the managed
  vector store: initiation of deployment, status views, and lifecycle
  actions, consistent with how the Dashboard surfaces other components
  (navigation, resource views, forms) per its architecture context.
- Feature-flag/gating consistent with existing Dashboard configuration
  conventions so the UI ships only with the managed posture.

- The Dashboard exposes a deploy-and-manage UI for the managed vector store
  (deploy, view status, manage) accessible to administrators.
- The UI is behind the platform's existing Dashboard feature-flag mechanism,
  disabled when the managed posture is not enabled.
- The integration follows the Dashboard's Kubernetes-CR-only interface
  pattern — no private component APIs.

  (deploy-and-manage UI for the managed path…)" — platform-managed branch

# Documentation for the platform-managed vector store posture

## Description

Author product documentation covering setup and limits for the
platform-managed vector store posture (operator-deployed Milvus with
productized images). This epic exists only if the posture investigation
selects the platform-managed path, and it runs after the managed-posture
implementation work has landed so the docs describe what was actually built.

## Scope

- New documentation topics for the managed posture: administrator setup
  (deploying the managed vector store through the Platform Operator),
  consuming it from Llama Stack RAG workloads, and the Dashboard
  deploy-and-manage flow.
- Documented limits: supported sizes/limits of the managed vector store,
  persistent storage constraints, and disconnected-environment guidance.
- Follow the Red Hat docs content process for authoring and publishing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Setup documentation exists for deploying and consuming the managed vector
  store end-to-end (operator deployment, Llama Stack RAG consumption,
  Dashboard management).
- Limits are documented explicitly, including storage and scale constraints
  of the managed offering.
- Documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented behavior
  (reviewed by the implementing teams), not just the strategy text.
- Documentation content is validated for accuracy against the platform
  architecture context.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-5 (P2)**: "Product documentation covers setup and limits for
  whichever posture ships" — platform-managed branch coverage.

# Decide the first supported vector store posture (platform-managed vs external-connection-only)

## Description

This investigation resolves the platform's single blocking decision for RAG
workloads: which vector store posture to productize first — a
platform-managed vector database (operator-deployed Milvus with productized
images and lifecycle) or an external-connection-only posture (data scientists
register an existing, externally operated vector store per project). The
strategy explicitly leaves this undecided, and the outcome determines the
existence and shape of all downstream implementation work for RAG vector
store integration.

## Scope

- Weigh both postures against the evaluation criteria named in the strategy:
  supportability cost, disconnected-environment viability, and
  time-to-market.
- Gather supporting evidence: the support model and image productization
  effort required for a managed Milvus offering; the disconnected/air-gapped
  viability of each posture; the connection requirements of common
  customer-managed vector stores (e.g., cloud vector DB services); and the
  relative delivery timelines.
- Produce a documented evaluation (not just a verdict) that stakeholders can
  audit, per the strategy's requirement for a documented decision record.
- Record a single, signed-off posture decision and identify which conditional
  implementation plan proceeds.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A written evaluation exists that compares platform-managed
  (operator-deployed Milvus) against external-connection-only on:
  supportability cost, disconnected-environment viability, and
  time-to-market.
- The evaluation states its evidence sources and assumptions.
- A single posture decision is recorded and signed off by the accountable
  product/architecture stakeholders.
- The decision record identifies which conditional downstream implementation
  path (managed or external-connection) is activated, so downstream planning
  can start immediately.
- Out-of-scope guardrail is respected: the decision covers only the *first*
  supported posture; shipping both postures in the same release remains out
  of scope.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: "A decision is reached, with a documented evaluation, on the
  first supported vector store posture: platform-managed (operator-deployed
  Milvus) versus external-connection-only." — fully covered by this
  investigation.
